title: So what really happened in four seventy-six?

post.caption: Ancient Rome, episode 14: did Rome really fall in AD 476? The boy emperor Romulus Augustus, Odoacer, and the half of the empire that carried on for another thousand years. Images: public domain / CC0 (Thomas Cole, Christen Købke, Karl Bryullov, Thomas Allom, American Numismatic Society). Map data: Natural Earth.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Every textbook says Rome fell in 476. It didn't.
beats.say: Every textbook says Rome fell in four seventy-six. It didn't.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So what really happened in 476?
beats.say: So what really happened in four seventy-six?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: In the bay of Naples stands the Castel dell'Ovo, the Egg Castle. On this spot, the last emperor of the West is said to have spent his retirement.
beats.say: In the bay of Naples stands the Castel dell Ovo, the Egg Castle. On this spot, the last emperor of the West is said to have spent his retirement.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Retirement? Who was he?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: A boy called Romulus Augustus, with the names of Rome's founder and its first emperor. People mocked him as Augustulus: little Augustus.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: His father, the general Orestes, had chased out the emperor before him and put the boy on the throne in 475.
beats.say: His father, the general Orestes, had chased out the emperor before him and put the boy on the throne in four seventy-five.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So who really ruled?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: The army. And the army in Italy was now mostly Germanic soldiers. Rome itself had already been sacked twice, in 410 and 455.
beats.say: The army. And the army in Italy was now mostly Germanic soldiers. Rome itself had already been sacked twice, in four ten and four fifty-five.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: What did the soldiers want?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Land in Italy. Orestes said no. So their officer, Odoacer, turned on him. Orestes was killed, and on 4 September 476, the boy was removed.
beats.say: Land in Italy. Orestes said no. So their officer, Odoacer, turned on him. Orestes was killed, and on the fourth of September, four seventy-six, the boy was removed.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Did they kill him too?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: No. Odoacer gave him a pension and sent him to live near Naples.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And Odoacer made himself emperor?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: He didn't. He had the emperor's regalia sent to Constantinople, to Zeno, the Roman emperor in the east, with a message: one emperor is enough.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So the Roman Empire didn't end?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Only in the west. The eastern half carried on from Constantinople, behind its huge walls, still calling itself the Roman Empire.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Even in the west, Julius Nepos, the emperor Orestes had chased out, still claimed the throne from Dalmatia until 480.
beats.say: Even in the west, Julius Nepos, the emperor Orestes had chased out, still claimed the throne from Dalmatia until four eighty.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: Then why do we say 476?
beats.say: Then why do we say four seventy-six?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: About forty years later, a chronicler in Constantinople wrote that the western empire ended with this boy. The date stuck.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: So when did Rome really end?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Nearly a thousand years later, in 1453.
beats.say: Nearly a thousand years later, in fourteen fifty-three.

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Like the video and follow History Sketches for the next episode: the last Roman emperor.

beats.speaker: q
beats.text: And tell us in the comments: when do you think Rome fell?

beats.speaker: a
beats.text: Fifteen hundred years later, ask anyone when Rome fell.
